subject: Animation
title: Jiří Trnka: The Czech Walt Disney
description: A 60-second lesson on Jiří Trnka: The Czech Walt Disney.

hook.text: Jiří Trnka was a Czech puppet filmmaker so influential that critics called him the Walt Disney of Eastern Europe.

buildup.text: Trnka directed elaborate puppet features in the 1940s and 1950s with stunning artistry and rich storytelling.

discovery.text: His film A Midsummer Night's Dream is considered one of the finest puppet animation features ever made.

twist.text: Trnka's final film, The Hand, was a political allegory so pointed that Communist authorities suppressed it.

climax.text: Trnka showed the world that puppet films could be as sophisticated and powerful as any live-action cinema.

punchline.text: Puppets in Prague challenged both Disney and dictators.

quiz.question: Why was Jiří Trnka called the Walt Disney of Eastern Europe?
options: He made exact copies of Disney films
He produced elaborate puppet animation features with stunning artistry that rivaled Disney's work
He opened a theme park in Prague
